author: Cinna Davis (OpenAI Codex assisted)
statement: A uniform Pauli/Walsh crossing construction makes the two exact flattening ranks the supports of a coefficient function and its transform, with integer factors and polynomially many symmetric pieces. A global invariant dual forces some piece in every coordinate-permutation-symmetric Pauli-diagonal decomposition to have both supports at least lambda!/((lambda-3k)!(k!)^3), k=floor(lambda/8), ruling out the accepted rho target in that class. The proof extends to color blocks and macro-alphabets; it does not rule out nonsymmetric or non-Pauli pieces, and no SAT improvement is established.
remaining_obligations: Independent review of the uniform construction and all-size support dual
A changed symmetry or operator class with a proved smaller eventual support rate; the same symmetric binary and two-bit macro classes are obstructed
All master-recursion and arbitrary-density costs for any genuinely improved successor
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent review claimed
